messages:
Maya: Quick pass on the stacked-area chart in console — users are misreading the normalization toggle. It defaulted to percent but many expect raw counts.
Alex: annoying. we should show a small unit pill on the axis when normalized: '100% (stacked)'. Also add tooltip text 'Normalized to 100% by timestamp'
Sam: suggestion: change label to 'Normalize: off | percent | per-node' instead of a ternary toggle. More discoverable.
Riley: UX nit: when percent is on, hovering a slice shows percent and raw value. important for ops.
Priya: accessibility: screen-reader summary should announce whether normalization is active and top contributor series for the selected timepoint. e.g., 'Normalization: percent. Top series: api-prod (42%).'
Maya: colors: request to bump contrast of the second area color — current green/teal pair fails AA at small legend swatches. Can we pick a palette with larger ΔL?
Alex: will prototype alt palette. Also propose dashed separators between stacked areas subtle 1px to aid thin slices.
Sam: smoothing discussion — spike smoothing currently uses simple moving average. For anomaly detection use-cases SG filter (Savitzky-Golay) preserves peaks better. Params idea: SG window=7 poly=2. Thoughts on perf?
Priya: SG ok but document fallback: if series length < window, disable smoothing. Also keyboard users should be able to toggle smoothing with a shortcut.
Riley: perf note: SG is O(n*window). For big dashboards we should do smoothing server-side or async client-side WebWorker.
Alex: agreed. frontend can do EMA for realtime live streams (cheap) and SG for historical charts (on-demand).
Maya: outliers: product owners prefer clipping display at a configurable percentile (99th) with an 'expand' affordance. But they want exported CSVs to keep raw numbers.
Sam: implement export: include columns 'display_value' and 'raw_value' and a boolean 'is_clipped'. That covers CSV consumers.
Priya: also include a legend badge 'clipped' when any series has clipped points, clicking opens a modal with list of timestamps and raw values. Make modal accessible.
Riley: keyboard: allow focus on legend items, Enter toggles, Shift+Enter toggles isolation (hide others). Also allow crosshair lock via 'L' key and announce to SR: 'Crosshair locked at 2026-03-01T12:00Z'.
Maya: microcopy for modal: 'Values above display range are clipped for readability. Use "Export raw" to download full data.'
Alex: small implementation detail: store per-chart settings in URL query param so team links preserve normalization/smoothing/clip settings.
Sam: I'll draft a tiny JSON config for chart state: { normalize: "percent", smoothing: "sg:7:2", clip_pct: 99 } and spec how URL encodes it.
Priya: accessibility extra: add live region updates when user toggles clipping so SR users know chart changed 'Clipping enabled at 99th percentile; 3 points clipped'.
ChartBot: Design doc: https://docs.redwood.com/designs/stacked-area-normalize-v2 — preview: https://staging.redwood.com/visuals/ux-2366
Maya: ok assigning Alex for palette + separators, Sam for export shape + smoothing spec, Priya for a11y review. Thanks all.
